🧠 Crypto News Brief: Soft U.S. jobs data flipped screens green, lifting Bitcoin back above $65K as Fed hike odds faded. But the relief is guarded — the Coldcard fallout still ripples on-chain and the CLARITY Act just slipped to September. 📈 Bitcoin reclaims $65K as weak U.S. jobs data cools the Fed A surprisingly soft U.S. July jobs report — just 23,000 payrolls added against the ~80,000 expected — pushed traders to price out a September Fed rate hike, sending risk assets higher. Bitcoin climbed back above $65,000, Strategy (MSTR) stock reclaimed $100, and global crypto market cap rose roughly 1% to about $2.21 trillion. Weaker labor data tends to favor rate cuts, which makes crypto more attractive to investors. Read full story → 🏛️ Senate opens CLARITY Act voting but punts final vote to September The U.S. Senate began the first procedural steps on the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act in an overnight session — the furthest the crypto market-structure bill has advanced. But leadership confirmed there will be no final vote before the August recess, pushing the decisive stretch to September amid unresolved Democratic concerns over ethics and illicit-finance provisions. More details → 🔓 Coldcard fallout: 210,000 BTC flees long-term holder wallets Roughly 210,000 BTC left long-term holder wallets in the week ending August 7 — the largest such outflow since December 2024 — as fallout from the Coldcard firmware exploit surfaced on-chain. Glassnode framed the move as forced custody migration to new wallets, ETFs, and regulated custodians rather than capitulation, with multisig setups unaffected. The exploit has drained more than $116 million since July 30. Read more → 🏦 Wintermute wins U.S. broker-dealer status in Wall Street push Crypto market maker Wintermute registered its New York unit, Wintermute USA, as a broker-dealer with the SEC and FINRA, giving one of digital assets' largest liquidity providers a regulated foothold in U.S. securities markets. The firm can now trade U.S. equities and options, act as an ETF authorized participant, and self-clear digital-asset securities for its own account — joining peers like Ripple and GSR in bridging crypto and traditional finance.
